title: Fashion Lookbook Photos and Outfit Ads
description: Create fashion lookbook photos for full outfits, fit and fabric detail. Choose try-ons, street walks or creator reviews for ads and product pages.
h1: Show complete looks in a fashion ad scene
lead: Use street-walk, try-on and creator-review formats to show how a collection fits and moves in real settings.
intro: A useful outfit ad shows the whole silhouette and the details shoppers want to compare. Start with a clear garment image, then choose a format for the collection.
tip: Upload each outfit as a full flat lay, top and bottom together, and choose one location for the whole collection so the images feel like one story.

steps.d: Include every garment you want to show and keep the full look inside the frame.
Name the location, light, and stance so each outfit belongs to the collection.
Download each photo, then add the collection name and garment details as text.

ideas.d: Post five or six looks as an Instagram carousel on the day a collection goes live.
Try the same outfit on a city street and on a seaside terrace to find the setting that matches your brand.
Style linen suits and slip dresses for summer weddings and garden parties.

faq.q: What should be in a lookbook source photo?
faq.a: Include the garments that make up the outfit and keep their shapes visible in the photo.

faq.q: How can a collection look connected?
faq.a: Reuse a location, light style, and crop across the outfits while showing each look clearly.

faq.q: Can the setting change between outfits?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a location that suits each collection and keep the framing consistent within it.

faq.q: How many outfits can one clip show?
faq.a: Focus on one full look per clip so the outfit reads clearly; make a second clip for another look.

faq.q: Can the setting change between looks?
faq.a: Use one location and light direction across the collection so the outfits feel like a set.

faq.q: What does a lookbook clip cost?
faq.a: A 10- or 15-second clip costs 40 or 60 credits.

overview.h2: Turn a Collection Into a Visual Story
overview.p: A lookbook frame does more than show a garment. It gives a launch a setting, pace, and point of view, so shoppers can understand how separate pieces belong together. Build each source as a complete outfit and repeat the visual language across the collection.

items.d: Lay out top, bottom, outer layer, shoes, and the accessory you intend to show together.
Photograph each piece flat and separated enough that a print, collar, or hem is not hidden by another garment.
Name the architecture, landscape, time of day, and attitude that can work for the next several looks.
Ask for relaxed standing, walking, or leaning rather than a pose that obscures the outfit.

results.h2: What a Lookbook Set Can Do

items.d: Give the outfit room to read from shoulder to shoe in one editorial frame.
Use styling and location to suggest how a collection works as a wardrobe.
Arrange several images for a carousel, email, or collection page.
Download the square image for commercial campaigns after checking the garments and scene.

scene_recipes.h2: Editorial Directions for a Seasonal Drop

items.d: Linen suit and sandals against pale stone arches with a glimpse of sea and warm late-afternoon light.
Coat, knit, and wide-leg trousers on a quiet concrete street after rain, with the full footwear visible.
Slip dress and lightweight jacket beside a garden path with soft daylight and a relaxed stance.
Sweater, denim, and crossbody bag in a bright cafe corner with a consistent neutral palette.

after_download.h2: Edit the Story Before You Share It

items.d: Make sure every featured piece matches the stock you can ship and the product names you publish.
Open with the hero look, then alternate silhouettes or color families so the carousel has rhythm.
Place dates, prices, product names, and collection links in the email or design tool after download.

good: Seasonal fashion drops with complete outfits
Editorial launches for apparel and accessories
Small catalogs that can share one location
not_ideal: A single item that needs a technical product shot
Outfits whose exact print alignment must be proven
A collection without enough source detail to identify each piece

visual.overview: Show a complete outfit on an adult model in a believable ad moment, with fit, movement or fabric detail easy to see.

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the garment and preserve its shape, color, and details. An adult wears the light beige tailored suit, smooths the jacket lapel once, and faces the camera with the full outfit visible. Full-body fashion photo, bright studio daylight, natural styling, no text or logos.

picker.title: Choose a fashion ad format
picker.lead: Pick a street walk, try-on or creator review to show how the outfit fits and moves.

cards.label: Street Walk: Pleated Skirt in Motion
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the garment and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult wears the pleated skirt mid-step on a sunlit city sidewalk, with the full outfit visible and the pleats lightly in motion. Full-body street-style still, natural daylight, clean storefront background, no text or logos.

cards.label: Creator Review: Work Bag Fit
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the bag and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult creator wears the messenger bag crossbody and turns slightly so the strap length and bag scale are clear. Three-quarter portrait, bright office daylight, casual creator-review still, no text or logos.

cards.label: GRWM: Knit Beanie for a Commute
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the beanie and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult wears the knit beanie and adjusts its edge before heading outside, with the fit around the face clear. Chest-up portrait, cool morning light, relaxed creator-style still, no text or logos.

cards.label: Outfit Transition: Beige Suit Fit
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the suit and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult model stands front-facing in the beige suit with the full silhouette and tailoring visible. Full-body eye-level fashion still, soft studio daylight, clean neutral background, no text or logos.

cards.label: Fabric Detail: Navy Blazer Cuff
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded garment as the exact product. Show a close detail of its navy blazer cuff, preserving the original fabric color and weave. Tight square crop with the seam and one button in focus, soft side daylight, no text or logos.

cards.label: Street Walk: Layered Workwear Look
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the outfit and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult wears the layered workwear look on a city block, pausing mid-stride so each garment remains visible. Full-body street-style still, soft overcast light, no text or logos.

cards.label: Creator Review: Navy Dress Fit
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the dress and keep its shape, color and details exactly. An adult creator wears the navy slip dress and turns slightly to show its drape and neckline. Three-quarter portrait, warm late-day light, natural creator-review still, no text or logos.

cards.label: Product Detail: Knit Sleeve
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the garment and keep its shape, color and details exactly. A hand gently pinches the knit sleeve so the weave and fabric drape are clear, with part of the worn outfit visible. Close fabric-detail still, soft directional daylight, no text or logos.
